summary: Accepted the beneficiary relationship from structural copper scarcity to Freeport-McMoRan with high confidence and high positive sensitivity. Current SEC-filed Q2 2026 evidence shows a direct path from realized copper pricing through mine margin and operating cash flow, while production recovery, costs, capex, minority interests, safety, Indonesian terms, commodity normalization, and valuation remain explicit limits. Updated the relationship page, catalog, log, and canonical relationship row; no strategy or follow-up operation was created because the current base and downside values remain below the market mark.

evidence.claim: The SEC-filed Q2 2026 results report a USD 6.17/lb realized copper price, USD 1.97/lb unit net cash cost, USD 2.048 billion of operating cash flow, and USD 1.104 billion of capital expenditure. They also report copper production of 786 million pounds versus 963 million a year earlier, demonstrating both direct copper-price transmission and material production-risk counterweights.

The current security review records a USD 62.72 mark and bounded 12-month downside and base comparisons of USD 32.64 and USD 47.36, or 48.0% and 24.5% below market, so the accepted causal edge does not justify strategy research or a signal.

The maintained idea defines the causal channel from constrained long-lead mine supply and copper demand to upstream producer economics, while explicitly preserving supply response, recycling, substitution, demand, cost, execution, jurisdiction, and valuation as contrary evidence.
